consumer:ny_it201.ask.city_resident@ny_i.question_phrase: a New York City resident ... for all of 2025
consumer:ny_it201.ask.city_resident@ny_i.source_phrase: p. 14, Line 50, "If you were a New York City resident for only part of 2025, complete Form IT-360.1"
consumer:ny_it201.ask.city_resident@ny_i.reason: A No is the part-year (or non-) City resident case line 50 sends to Form IT-360.1; the gate refuses it.

consumer:ny_it201.ask.it225@ny_it201i:p7.question_phrase: any other New York addition or subtraction on Form IT-225
consumer:ny_it201.ask.it225@ny_it201i:p7.source_phrase: p. 7, Step 4, "See below and Form IT-225, New York State Modifications, and its instructions."
consumer:ny_it201.ask.it225@ny_it201i:p7.reason: The question asks whether any IT-225 modification applies, which is what p. 7 and the line 23 and 31 instructions (p. 8, p. 10) send to Form IT-225.

consumer:ny_it201.ask.itemize@ny_it201i:.question_phrase: itemize deductions on your New York return (Form IT-196)
consumer:ny_it201.ask.itemize@ny_it201i:.source_phrase: p. 11, "To calculate your New York itemized deduction, use Form IT-196"
consumer:ny_it201.ask.itemize@ny_it201i:.reason: The question asks whether the filer itemizes on Form IT-196, the case p. 11 describes; the gate refuses it.

consumer:ny_it201.ask.owes_use_tax@ny_it.question_phrase: owe New York sales or use tax on purchases made without paying New York tax
consumer:ny_it201.ask.owes_use_tax@ny_it.source_phrase: p. 19, "If you do not owe any sales or use tax, you must enter 0 on line 59."
consumer:ny_it201.ask.owes_use_tax@ny_it.reason: A No is the case p. 19 says to enter 0 for; the question restates p. 18's "You owe sales or compensating use tax if you" conditions.

consumer:ny_it201.ask.abroad@ny_it201i:p.question_phrase: Were you outside the United States and Puerto Rico on April 15, 2026, and are you using the extra time to file that this gives?
consumer:ny_it201.ask.abroad@ny_it201i:p.source_phrase: If you qualify for one or more of the special conditions below, enter the specified two-character code.
consumer:ny_it201.ask.abroad@ny_it201i:p.reason: The item G introduction on p. 5 defines no condition; the code this answer stands for is defined on p. 6, which the question cites, and the reader only tests whether any item G code applies.

consumer:ny_it201.ask.installment@ny_it2.question_phrase: If you owe New York tax, will you ask to pay it in installments?
consumer:ny_it201.ask.installment@ny_it2.source_phrase: If you qualify for one or more of the special conditions below, enter the specified two-character code.
consumer:ny_it201.ask.installment@ny_it2.reason: The item G introduction on p. 5 defines no condition; the installment code is defined on p. 6, which the question cites, and the reader only tests whether any item G code applies.

consumer:ny_it201.ask.city_resident@ny_i.question_phrase: a New York City resident (the Bronx, Brooklyn, Manhattan, Queens or Staten Island) for all of 2025
consumer:ny_it201.ask.city_resident@ny_i.source_phrase: If you were a New York State resident for only part of the year, do not file Form IT-201.
consumer:ny_it201.ask.city_resident@ny_i.reason: New York City lies in New York State, so a resident of the city for all of 2025 by the State's test was a State resident for all of 2025; the gate treats a city Yes as a full-year State resident and asks the State question after a No.

consumer:ny_it201.ask.city_resident@ny_i.question_phrase: by the same test with New York City in place of New York State
consumer:ny_it201.ask.city_resident@ny_i.source_phrase: Your domicile is New York State.
consumer:ny_it201.ask.city_resident@ny_i.reason: The question applies the page's domicile and permanent-place-of-abode tests with the city in place of the State, and a city domicile or a city abode with the days in the city meets the State's tests, so a Yes is a State resident; a No leads to the State question itself.

consumer:ny_it201.ask.spouse_itemizes@ny.question_phrase: Is your husband or wife itemizing deductions on their own New York return?
consumer:ny_it201.ask.spouse_itemizes@ny.source_phrase: You may take either the New York standard deduction or the New York itemized deduction.
consumer:ny_it201.ask.spouse_itemizes@ny.reason: Page 10 states only the choice between the two deductions; the married-filing-separately rule the answer serves is on p. 11, which the question cites, and the gate asks it only of a separate return.
